definition: A TargetRollout is the act of deploying an artifact against a destination in a tier, as one part of a Deployment. The destination itself is identified by the TargetRollout's target, and the logical environment it belongs to by its tier.
notes: A TargetRollout carries a deploymentId reference back to its parent Deployment
A TargetRollout represents the rollout to a single destination, not the destination itself
failureType is available on targetRollout.finished to express per-destination failure reasons
TargetRollout makes "what was rolled out to a tier, and where" a direct query, rather than an inference over Service's backwards-pointing environment reference
examples: Rolling myapp@sha256:0b31b1c0 out to the us-east-1 cluster within the production tier
Shifting a canary slot to a new version as part of a blue/green deployment
Deploying a release to a named deployment slot in a cloud provider region
counterExamples: A destination such as a cluster, region or canary slot (that is the target)
The aggregate deployment across all targets (that is a Deployment)
